offender.name: John Wayne Gacy
offender.caption: People v. Gacy, 103 Ill. 2d 1 (1984) · Circuit Court of Cook County

vitals.v: 33 counts of murder, one count of deviate sexual assault, one count of indecent liberties with a child, one count of aggravated kidnaping (dismissed at trial)
Guilty on all murder counts after a single jury trial in Cook County
Death on 12 counts (murders after the 1977 death-penalty statute); natural life on each of the remaining 21
29 bodies recovered from the crawl space and grounds of 8213 W. Summerdale; four from the Des Plaines and Illinois rivers

sources.title: People v. Gacy, 103 Ill. 2d 1, 468 N.E.2d 1171
sources.note: Direct appeal; affirms the convictions and sentences. Opening paragraph recites the counts, verdict and sentences.

proceedings.label: Convicted on 33 counts of murder
proceedings.pinpoint: 103 Ill. 2d 1, opening paragraph of the opinion
proceedings.note: Verdict date is not stated in the opinion; the opinion affirming was filed 1984-06-06.

attributions.note: The court record and the attributed total coincide: 33 bodies recovered, 33 counts.

claims.subject: offender
claims.note: Admission during the investigation, as recited by the court.

events.text: Robert Piest, 15, leaves the Nisson Pharmacy in Des Plaines to meet a building contractor about a summer job and is never seen alive again. Gacy’s truck is seen outside the pharmacy.
Search warrant issued for Gacy, his home at 8213 W. Summerdale and three PDM vehicles.
Excavation of the crawl space and grounds recovers 29 bodies; four more are recovered from the Des Plaines and Illinois rivers.
Illinois Supreme Court affirms the convictions and the death sentences on direct appeal.
